published_price: Free without a key; $1.95 per 1,000 lookups with one, prepaid from $10, first 100 free
chart_assumptions: Keyed plan; first 100 free excluded. The measured run enabled all configured providers with Geocodio’s quota exhausted; production quotas and budgets can change coverage.
pricing_method: Our own price. Without a key, lookups use only our own geocoders and cost nothing. With a key they may also use commercial geocoders, at $1.95 per 1,000 lookups that return a rate; declined addresses aren't charged.

published_price: Free on your own server: $0 with only its own geocoders (Nominatim, Photon, Pelias), or the providers' prices for any commercial geocoders you add keys for
pricing_method: No fee from us. Provider counts below are scaled to 1,000 lookups from a 309-address run, not raw counts for 309 addresses. For example, 78 Geocodio calls ÷ 309 × 1,000 ≈ 252. This models the observed provider mix at the listed unit prices, not a maximum or an invoice. Different addresses, retries, storage rights and provider plans change the cost; HERE’s current public page does not expose its unit rate.

chart_assumptions: PAYG $0.50 per 1,000 requests, no monthly fee. At 2,000 lookups/month: $1.00/month. The separate free plan and subscription capacity prices are not used for this point. Full street-address inputs on the same 277 officially labeled evalA cases.
pricing_method: PAYG has no monthly fee. Starter: $9 ÷ 100,000 × 1,000 = $0.09 only when fully used. Benchmarked with full street addresses on the same 277 officially labeled evalA cases; see the measured accuracy column. Low subscription unit prices depend on utilization.

published_price: Developer $59/mo for 100,000 calls; $39/mo with annual billing
pricing_method: $59 ÷ 100,000 × 1,000. Sales tax documentation accepts street_address with city and state; combined rates and commercial use require a paid plan. Developer disallows data caching/storage. Not benchmarked; street input alone does not establish rooftop accuracy.

Basic: $9.99 ÷ 10,000 × 1,000 ≈ $1.00; Advanced: $19.99 ÷ 100,000 × 1,000 ≈ $0.20. The vendor describes US ZIP-level lookups. Public pages are old; current availability and billing need confirmation. Not benchmarked.

Starter: $19 ÷ 2,000 × 1,000 = $9.50. Extra requests: $5 ÷ 5,000 × 1,000 = $1, plus the plan fee. Enterprise is $199 for 100,000 ($1.99 per 1,000 at capacity). Documentation requires state and 5-digit ZIP, not a street address. Not benchmarked.
$0.05 × 1,000, using the Calculations API alone. With the Transaction API, each $0.50 transaction includes 10 calculations.

Growth is $29/month and overage starts at $0.0242/call ($24.20 per 1,000 extra calls). The public page does not tie an included call allowance to this price; the calculator’s default 15,000 must not be treated as the allowance. The free plan advertises 100 calls/month; our account stopped after 100 total.

$83 ÷ 10,000 API calls on Business, fully used. Startup is $41 for up to 2,500 API calls ($16.40 per 1,000 at capacity); Hobby is $24 for 250 ($96 per 1,000). These are different utilization scenarios, not the bill for 1,000 calls.

chart_assumptions: Historical illustration: $79/month ÷ 2,000 × 1,000 from the 21 October reading. Current page exposes no price; API allowance needs confirmation.
pricing_method: $79 ÷ 2,000 lookups. The price is from our 2026-10-21 reading; on 2026-10-22 the page showed order tiers without prices.

chart_assumptions: $99/month Professional, 200 orders = 2,000 rate lookups; no imported orders. Full monthly allowance used.
pricing_method: $99 ÷ 2,000 lookups, on Professional, the cheapest plan with the API.

chart_assumptions: Illustration only: $699/year for ONE paid state ÷ 12 ÷ 2,000 × 1,000. Nationwide API access and contract cost are not established.
pricing_method: The published $699/year is per state for a compliance bundle, equivalent to $58.25/month. At 2,000 lookups/month in one paid state, that is $29.13 per 1,000. It is not a nationwide API quote; API eligibility and state coverage need confirmation. The old rates-by-address documentation URL now redirects to generic developer navigation, so it no longer substantiates a free production API.

published_price: €20 per 5,000 extra transactions, plus a plan fee
pricing_method: 10 lookups count as one transaction, so €20 covers 50,000 lookups past the plan's allowance. The plan fee isn't published. Lovat is now called Lappa.

published_price: $29.99/mo for 200,000 credits (2 per call); free plan 200 credits a month
chart_assumptions: Separate sample: 76/87 correct (87.4%), ZIP-code input only; not the 277-address evalA sample, so excluded from frontier ranking. Starter is $29.99/month for 200,000 credits, at 2 credits/call. At the chart’s 2,000 lookups/month: $29.99 ÷ 2 = $14.995 per 1,000. The $0.30 figure requires using all 100,000 included calls.
pricing_method: $29.99 ÷ 100,000 calls on Starter, the vendor's own figure. Larger plans come to $0.20 and $0.15. The API takes a 5-digit ZIP code.

published_price: $50 per market per month for ecommerce; $100 otherwise
pricing_method: Starter costs $50 per market per month for ecommerce and $100 otherwise. At 1,000 lookups/month in one market, that is $50–100 per 1,000; at 10,000, $5–10. Each registered US state is a separate market. API eligibility and high-volume fees depend on contract; this is not a nationwide API quote.
$1,500 ÷ 12,000 lookups, for the street-address database. The ZIP-level one is $389 a year.
